name: mc_undo_control
description: Note: automatic Undo is off by default. On Education 1.26.x, once it is on, the native check before the first build makes the game command channel stop responding for good (the player's typing gets no response either) until Minecraft is restarted; configure enabled=true only when the user explicitly asks for it. action=status only reads the automatic Undo state and timings; configure turns it on or off and sets the block budget (default 4096, max 32768); same-material ranges are saved as whole regions and compared with native region checks. clear releases this server's backups. Backups live only in game memory, with no disk backup and no Redo. Turning automatic backup off clears the old history.

name: mc_undo
description: Undo the last protected setblock/fill or build tool call; several build commands count as one step. All target blocks are checked first, then each region is restored with conditional commands so later changes are not overwritten. operationId guards against undoing the wrong version. Use overwriteChanges only when the user explicitly asks to overwrite conflicts, or accepts restoring the site after an operation whose outcome is uncertain; never set it to true on your own. This first version covers basic Overworld building blocks only: no mobs, inventories, water flow or redstone chains outside the region, and no Redo. Do not switch worlds or dimensions while it runs.

name: mc_status
description: Report the WebSocket bridge, whether the game is answering commands (commandState), the last reply and timeout times, the /connect command and subscribed events. connected only means the network link is up; timed-out means a recent command got no reply, so do not assume the game can still act. No side effects.

name: mc_await_connection
description: Block until the game connects to the bridge, for at most timeoutSeconds seconds. A timeout is not an error; it just reports connected=false. Call it after asking the user to type /connect.

name: mc_run_command
description: Send one raw slash command, for anything this server has no dedicated tool for. Single line only, no newline chaining. Refuses wsserver / connect / closewebsocket, including when wrapped in execute (that would cut this bridge). The leading slash is optional.

command.description: For example "time set day" or "/give @s diamond 1"

name: mc_run_commands
description: Send several raw commands in order; each one passes the command policy on its own. Good for hand-written macros; for many blocks use mc_build_shape or mc_build_blueprint, which merge them into the fewest fill commands automatically.

reportFailuresOnly.description: Return only the failed commands and skip the successful ones. Per-command results of a large batch (for example 200 fill commands) easily run past ten thousand tokens, and most of them just say "N blocks filled"; turn this on for large batches when you do not need each number. The issued / succeeded / failed counts are not affected.

name: mc_agent_create
description: Spawn the Agent next to the player. Calling it again when the Agent already exists is safe. The Agent is the robot found only in Education Edition; summon it with mc_agent_create first. Directions are relative to the way the Agent faces, not world directions.

name: mc_agent_move
description: Move the Agent steps blocks in a direction, one command per block. A step blocked by a block fails without stopping the rest. The Agent is the robot found only in Education Edition; summon it with mc_agent_create first. Directions are relative to the way the Agent faces, not world directions.

name: mc_analyze_symmetry
description: Check whether a region is symmetric left to right (or front to back), and when it is not, point out **which parts** are not. Use it to grade student builds: the score is the share of symmetric cells, not a gut feeling. How it works: testforblocks only compares by translation, never mirrored, so a mirrored copy is made first with the mirror option of structure save / load and then compared with the original. Warning: this **temporarily writes** to the scratch area: its contents are always backed up first and restored right after the comparison; if the backup fails, it stops without touching the world. scratch must not overlap the analyzed region, or the mirrored copy overwrites the original build. The region is limited by the structure command (64x384x64).

name: mc_read_block
description: Report what is actually at a coordinate, without you having to guess first. Education has no command to read a block, so this runs testforblock with air as a sentinel; when the guess is wrong, the game message names the actual block. Note: it returns the **localized display name** (for example "Dirt", or "泥土" in a Chinese game), not the block ID (dirt), so it cannot be fed back to mc_set_block; to check by ID, use mc_test_block. The message format has no official guarantee; when it cannot be parsed, this tool returns an error with the raw message instead of guessing.

mode.description: absolute = world coordinates; relative = ~ relative to the command source; local = ^ relative to its facing

name: mc_verify_reading
description: Block reading relies on the testforblock **failure message** revealing the block name, and that message format has no official stability guarantee. When a game update changes the wording, or the game language is not Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese or English, parsing breaks, and it breaks **silently**. This probe actively checks whether the reading path still works; **run it once before class** to know whether mc_read_block results can be trusted. It does not need to know what is at the spot: if it is air, it asks about bedrock (a guaranteed mismatch) to force a failure message; if something is there, the first question already produced a message. At most two commands, and it never writes to the world. parseable=false means the protocol has drifted, and mc_read_block results cannot be trusted at all.

name: mc_compare_regions

Comparing block by block hits the MCP host timeout beyond a few hundred blocks; this does not. masked=true ignores air in the source region and only checks that what should be there is there, regardless of anything extra around it; masked=false requires an exact match. Both regions must be the same size; destination is the minimum corner of the target region.

name: mc_structure
description:
Save a region as a named structure, or place a saved structure back into the world. This is the official way to keep what the AI built, mass-produce it, or take it to another world.

**Choose saveMode by what the user wants; do not always use the same one:**
- `memory` (default) = temporary storage for this connection. Use it while the AI keeps revising the same build: save a version to keep a way back, and load it if a change goes wrong. It disappears when the game closes and leaves no files on disk.
- `disk` = only when **the user explicitly says to keep it** ("remember this building", "save it so I can use it next time"). It is written as a file into the game world folder and survives closing the game, which really leaves something on the user disk, so do not write it when they did not ask to keep it.

Versioning is **naming**: `castle_v1`, `castle_v2`. The same name overwrites without warning, so change the name before saving a new version. The game has no command to list saved structures, so names are the only record; mc_status lists the ones saved during this connection.

name.description: Versions are told apart by this; the same name overwrites

name: mc_build_shape
description:
Build a shape directly in the world. Block coordinates are merged into the fewest fill commands automatically, so a sphere of radius 20 takes a few hundred commands instead of thirty thousand.
[Choose a shape by intent]
Basic volumes: box, sphere, ellipsoid, cylinder, cone (topRadius>0 makes a truncated cone), pyramid (sides sets the number of sides, topRadius>0 makes a frustum), prism (regular n-sided prism).
Lines and surfaces: line (straight line), curve (smooth curve), disk (disk / ring), tube (cylinder in any direction).
Building parts: wedge (single slope), roof (gable / hip), arch, stairs (straight stairs), spiralStairs, polywall (polyline wall / city wall).
Terrain and paths: heightfield (rolling ground), ribbon (road / bridge deck).
Decoration and forms: torus (ring), helix, cross (plus-shaped column), star (star-shaped column), revolution (solid of revolution).

[Easy to confuse; read this first]
Slanted columns, beams, pipes -> tube, not cylinder (cylinder only aligns with x / y / z).
Walls or fences with right-angle turns -> polywall, not curve (curve is smooth and rounds off right angles).
A roof with a ridge -> roof; a single slope or ramp only -> wedge.
Stairs that wind around a tower -> spiralStairs; straight up and down -> stairs.
Tower bodies, bases or chimneys that are wider at one end -> cone or pyramid with topRadius, not stacked layers of box.
Domes, vases, paraboloids, cooling towers and other round forms whose width changes -> revolution with a different profile; no other shape is needed.
A stretch of rolling ground -> heightfield; a flat road with a width -> ribbon.

If unsure, check the block count and bounding box with mc_build_preview first; it does not touch the world.

All coordinates are absolute world coordinates; if you do not know where the player is, call mc_query_target first. Building changes the world directly, so check the block count and bounding box with the matching preview tool before you build.

name: mc_events_catalog
description: Return the event names known to work. Mojang does not formally document this list, so subscribing to a name outside it is allowed; it is just marked unverified. No side effects.

name: mc_events_subscribe
description: Start receiving a kind of game event (for example PlayerMessage for chat, BlockPlaced for placed blocks, PlayerTravelled for movement). Events go into a ring buffer; read them later with mc_events_poll. This is how the AI perceives what the player is doing. Subscriptions are renewed automatically after a reconnect.

name: mc_events_unsubscribe
description: Stop receiving a kind of event. Events already in the buffer are kept.

name: mc_events_poll
description: Return the events after a cursor. Use afterCursor=0 the first time, then pass back the nextCursor from the previous call to keep reading. dropped greater than 0 means the buffer wrapped around and some events are lost for good; poll more often. No side effects.

eventName.description: Only return this kind of event
